10. Differentiation

From the definition of the derivative through the mean value theorem, l'Hôpital, and Taylor expansions.

  • Differentiable Implies Continuous — Differentiable implies continuous, but not conversely — zoom into the corner of ∣x∣|x|∣x∣ and it never flattens. The first step of the differentiation scenes.
  • A Discontinuous Derivative — f(x)=x2sin⁡(1/x)f(x) = x^2\sin(1/x)f(x)=x2sin(1/x) (f(0)=0f(0) = 0f(0)=0) is differentiable everywhere with f′(0)=0f'(0) = 0f′(0)=0, yet the derivative f′(x)=2xsin⁡(1/x)−cos⁡(1/x)f'(x) = 2x\sin(1/x) - \cos(1/x)f′(x)=2xsin(1/x)−cos(1/x) oscillates and is discontinuous at 000. Differentiable does not imply continuously differentiable — though derivatives still keep the intermediate value property (Darboux).
  • The Secant Meets Its Parallel Tangent — Somewhere on the curve, a tangent is parallel to the secant of slope f(b)−f(a)b−a\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}b−af(b)−f(a)​. Drag ξ\xiξ to find it.
  • Derivative Sign and Monotonicity — The sign of f′f'f′ decides where the curve rises and falls: up on the green background (f′>0f' > 0f′>0), down on the red one (f′<0f' < 0f′<0). Drag x0x_0x0​ and watch the tangent's color track the sign — one step behind the Mean Value Theorem.

  • Cauchy's Mean Value Theorem — On the parametric curve (g(t),f(t))(g(t), f(t))(g(t),f(t)) a tangent parallel to the chord exists. For f(t)=t2f(t) = t^2f(t)=t2, g(t)=t3g(t) = t^3g(t)=t3 it sits at ξ=14/9\xi = 14/9ξ=14/9.
  • L'Hôpital's Rule — In a 0/00/00/0 or ∞/∞\infty/\infty∞/∞ form, differentiating the numerator and the denominator keeps the limit. Drive xxx toward the limit point and watch f(x)g(x)\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}g(x)f(x)​ track f′(x)g′(x)\frac{f'(x)}{g'(x)}g′(x)f′(x)​.
  • Darboux's Theorem — Derivatives have the intermediate value property even when discontinuous — f′(x)=2xsin⁡(1/x)−cos⁡(1/x)f'(x) = 2x\sin(1/x) - \cos(1/x)f′(x)=2xsin(1/x)−cos(1/x) oscillates wildly near 0 yet steps on every level. Jump discontinuities are impossible in a derivative.
  • The Weierstrass Function — W(x)=∑n=0∞ancos⁡(bnπx)W(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a^n\cos(b^n\pi x)W(x)=∑n=0∞​ancos(bnπx) — continuous everywhere yet differentiable nowhere. The M-test scene powers the continuity argument, and the graph turns thornier as partial sums grow. The full nowhere-differentiability proof is idea-level only.
  • Polynomials Hugging the Curve — Lay the Maclaurin polynomial Tn(x)T_n(x)Tn​(x) over sin⁡x\sin xsinx. Raise the degree and watch it hug the curve.
  • Taylor's Theorem: The Remainder Envelope — The error Rn(x)R_n(x)Rn​(x) is trapped in the band Tn(x)±∣x∣n+1/(n+1)!T_n(x) \pm |x|^{n+1}/(n+1)!Tn​(x)±∣x∣n+1/(n+1)!. Raise nnn and the band shrinks to zero.
  • Convex Functions — Convex when the chord floats above the graph — for differentiable fff this is the same as f′f'f′ increasing, and the second derivative decides it. Up to Jensen's inequality.
  • Riding Tangents to the Root — Ride the tangent down to the root. The number of correct digits doubles each step.
  • The Contraction Cobweb — The cobweb between y=xy = xy=x and y=f(x)y = f(x)y=f(x) gets sucked into one point. The error shrinks like qnq^nqn.
